I'll start by fixing the cross-section of the leak channel in the axial (r,z) plane, since everything else is that section swept along the thread helix.

**Interpretation I'm adopting** (stated up front as it drives the whole build): the lid bottoms out on the neck's crest flats (that's the seal that makes the leak path *helical* rather than a full annular shell), and everywhere else — both flanks and the root — the lid surface stands off the neck surface by a constant 0.2 mm measured normal to the flank. So the channel section is a 0.2 mm band wrapped over flank–root–flank, closed at each crest corner by a 0.2 mm radial strip.

```python
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt, os

# --- given by the request ---
OD      = 0.040      # m, neck outside diameter
PITCH   = 0.002      # m
DEPTH   = 0.001      # m, thread depth
HTHREAD = 0.012      # m, threaded neck height
GAP     = 0.0002     # m, clearance on every flank

# --- chosen by me (not stated in the request) ---
CREST_FLAT = 0.0005  # m, axial width of the crest flat (contact land)
ROOT_FLAT  = 0.0005  # m, axial width of the root flat
# -> flank axial run = (PITCH - CREST_FLAT - ROOT_FLAT)/2

r_c, r_r = OD/2, OD/2 - DEPTH
run = (PITCH - CREST_FLAT - ROOT_FLAT)/2
zA  = CREST_FLAT/2
A  = np.array([r_c, zA])                 # upper crest corner
P1 = np.array([r_r, zA + run])           # root corner
P2 = np.array([r_r, zA + run + ROOT_FLAT])
B  = np.array([r_c, zA + 2*run + ROOT_FLAT])  # next crest corner

def outward_normal(p, q):                # solid lies to the -r / tooth side
    d = (q - p)/np.linalg.norm(q - p)
    return np.array([d[1], -d[0]])
n1, n2, n3 = outward_normal(A,P1), outward_normal(P1,P2), outward_normal(P2,B)

def inter(p, dp, q, dq):
    t = np.linalg.solve(np.column_stack([dp, -dq]), q - p)[0]
    return p + t*dp
A1 = A + GAP*n1
Q1 = inter(A1, P1-A, P1+GAP*n2, P2-P1)
Q2 = inter(P1+GAP*n2, P2-P1, P2+GAP*n3, B-P2)
B3 = B + GAP*n3

print("flank angle from radial: %.2f deg" % np.degrees(np.arctan2(run, DEPTH)))
print("A ",A," P1",P1," P2",P2," B ",B)
print("A1",A1," Q1",Q1," Q2",Q2," B3",B3)
print("section axial span %.4f mm (pitch %.1f mm)" % (1e3*(B[1]-A[1]), 1e3*PITCH))
print("perp gap check, flank1 %.4f mm, root %.4f mm, flank2 %.4f mm" % (
    1e3*np.dot(A1-A,n1), 1e3*np.dot(Q1-P1,n2), 1e3*np.dot(B3-B,n3)))

poly = np.array([A,P1,P2,B,B3,Q2,Q1,A1,A])
plt.figure(figsize=(5,5)); plt.plot(1e3*poly[:,0],1e3*poly[:,1],'o-')
plt.gca().set_aspect('equal'); plt.xlabel('r [mm]'); plt.ylabel('z [mm]'); plt.grid(True)
plt.title('leak-channel section'); plt.show()
```

Section is exact: 0.2000 mm normal gap on both flanks and the root, 1.5 mm axial span inside a 2 mm pitch, so the 0.5 mm crest land seals between turns. Now the gmsh geometry — three transfinite quads forming the band, helically twist-extruded about z. Coarse layer count first.
Twist-extrude all three quads in one call so shared internal curves are swept once; inspect the returned entity list before looping.

Shared laterals are reused (tags 23, 45 appear twice), and each block is `[top, volume, lat0..lat3]`. Verify the lateral ordering positively against the analytic swept midpoint of each edge rather than trusting it.

x, y match the half-angle swept midpoint exactly for every edge — the ordering is confirmed (the z discrepancy is just where gmsh puts the parametric mid, a constant dz/2). Tighten the check to that and run the remaining 20 chunks.

Argument order bug: `geo.twist` takes the axis **point** first and the translation second, so I built a pure rotation (bbox z never left 0.25–1.75). Rebuild the model from scratch with the correct order.
Exactly 12.000 mm of thread height. Now physical groups (inner end = top, the jar-mouth side; outer end = bottom, open air), then the surface mesh.

Surface mesh is all quads. Now an analytic point-in-channel test (unwrap the helix, test the section polygon) so each exported triangle can be wound outward from the fluid by construction rather than by guesswork.
Inside test agrees on all five probes. Now export one STL per patch to `constant/triSurface`, with every triangle flipped to face out of the fluid.
Per-triangle orientation was applied, so let me verify closure and winding of the union of the four patches directly, the way the advisory checks will.
696 free edges = 696 same-direction duplicates, so some triangles are still wound the wrong way. Locate them.

Faceting was the real issue, not the winding: at 8 layers per quarter turn the chord sagitta at r=20 mm is ~0.1 mm, half the gap itself. Rebuild with 32 layers/quarter (≈1 mm arc, 6 µm sagitta) and get a volume mesh on disk.
Now the OpenFOAM case: msh v2.2, a minimal system dict set, `gmshToFoam`, `checkMesh`.
All four patches populated (16 168 boundary faces, `defaultFaces` empty and dropped). Run checkMesh.

checkMesh: **Mesh OK** — 13 440 hexes, max aspect 10.3, max skewness 0.99, max non-orthogonality 28.4. The STLs on disk are from the discarded coarse model, so re-export them from this one (eps raised above the 6 µm faceting error).
Union of the four patch STLs is watertight (0 free edges) and consistently wound. Now look at the thing.
Camera was inside the part. Frame it automatically instead.
Shape is right: a 5.25-turn ribbon, neck side inboard, lid side outboard. Now measure the requested numbers off the built geometry.

Two of those measurements are artefacts of how I probed, not of the geometry (nearest *vertex* rather than nearest surface; and an unwrap that ignores that each angle carries 5–6 turns). Redo both properly.
Stray cell; here is the real one.

Gap measures 0.1999–0.2040 mm over the 25th–100th percentile (the lower 5 % are facets next to the crest-corner strips, where the nearest lid surface is the strip itself), and the crest helical residual `z − p·θ/2π` collapses onto exactly two values, 0.25 and 1.75 mm, over all 5.25 turns — the lead is exactly 2.000 mm. Now refine from 2 to 4 cells across the gap and re-mesh.
